title: Resume data
description: The single source of truth for your resume. build/build.py reads this, measures it in a browser, solves the page layout and prints the PDF. You never edit HTML.

name.description: Your name, split in two because the design styles them differently — the last name is set bolder than the first. Optional here: if data/_profile.yml supplies it, omit it and this file inherits it. The build still fails if neither provides one.

first.description: Given name, shown in the lighter weight.

role.description: Optional subtitle under your name — usually the role you are applying for. Delete the line entirely for no subtitle.

contact.description: Contact details, rendered top-right on page 1. Usually lives in data/_profile.yml instead, since it is the same on every application. Setting it here overrides that file entirely — including the whole `rows` list, which replaces rather than adds to it.

address.description: Shown on its own line. Usually just 'City, State' — a street address is rarely wanted on a resume.

rows.description: Clickable contact lines. Use an empty list if you want only an address.

meta.description: Document-level settings. These reach the PDF's metadata and the layout solver, not the visible page. 'lang' and 'maxPages' normally come from data/_profile.yml; 'description' names the target role, so it belongs to this document.

description.description: One sentence, stamped into the PDF's metadata. Some applicant tracking systems read it.

maxPages.description: The hard ceiling the layout solver works under. It will fit your content into this many pages or fail loudly — it will never silently truncate. Normally omitted here and inherited from data/_profile.yml; set it here only to override that for this one document.

lang.description: BCP 47 language tag, e.g. 'en-US'. Stamped into the PDF so screen readers pronounce it correctly.

sidebar.description: The narrow left column. Blocks flow down it and split across pages automatically.

blocks.description: Sidebar blocks, rendered top to bottom in this order.

mainColumn.description: The wide right column. Exactly one summary, one experience and one education section, in whatever order you list them.

id.description: Kebab-case identifier: lowercase letters and digits, single hyphens between. Must be unique. It becomes the HTML id and the key the layout solver uses to place this entry, so changing it invalidates a solved layout.

href.description: What clicking it does. 'tel:+15551234567' opens the dialer, 'mailto:you@example.com' opens mail, 'https://...' opens a site.

type.description: 'list' is a column of lines with optional group headings. 'details' is a label/value table, e.g. for licenses or clearances.

heading.description: The block's visible heading, e.g. 'Key Skills'.

items.description: Each entry is either a plain line of text, or a group heading written as 'group: Heading Text' to label the lines beneath it.

oneOf.description: A single line in the list.

rows.description: Label/value pairs, rendered as a two-column table.

href.description: Optional — makes the value a link.

type.description: Which section this is. Exactly one of each must appear in mainColumn.

heading.description: The visible heading, e.g. 'Work Experience'. Rename it freely; the 'type' above is what the build keys off.

text.description: A single paragraph. Supports **bold** and *italic*. Use a YAML folded block ('>-') so you can wrap it across lines without inserting line breaks into the output.

jobs.description: Your roles, newest first. The solver may split a job's bullets across a page break, but never orphans its header.

subtitle.description: A second line under the title — dates, honors, field of study.

title.description: Role and employer, e.g. 'Operations Lead, Acme Coffee'.

date.description: The dates as you want them printed, e.g. 'Mar 2019 – Aug 2021'. Free text — it is never parsed.

datetime.description: Machine-readable start date for the HTML <time> element, e.g. '2019-03'. Not shown to the reader.

location.description: Where the job was, e.g. 'Springfield, IL'. Omit on a gap entry.

gap.description: Set true to render this as a career-gap entry: italic title, no location, no bullets. Must be unquoted true or false — 'true' in quotes is a string, and every non-empty string counts as true.

bullets.description: Achievement lines. Required unless 'gap: true'. Supports **bold** and *italic*. Lead with the result, not the responsibility.
